contentSections.heading: Quick answer
paragraphs: Yes, with a caveat. On October 24, 2026, Hostinger had a TrustScore of 4.6 from 73,411 Trustpilot reviews and answered 99% of the negative ones. The company invites customers to review, which pushes the average up, and the most cited complaints are AI support, billing and renewal. On hosting, billing calls for attention to automatic renewal; see below how to turn it off. The 20% off the first period comes from the [SONAR20 Hostinger coupon](/en/coupons/hostinger).

postParagraphs: The screenshots are from October 19, 2026, and the table from October 24: the score was the same, the response rate to negative reviews went from 98% to 99%, and the percentages per star did not move.
The sample covered reviews in several languages, so the score is global, not the opinion of one market.
What the table does not show is who gets invited and who writes on their own. That is where the next chapter starts.

contentSections.heading: Three readings that change the math
paragraphs: To see what sits behind the 4.6, the 100 most recent one-star reviews and the 100 most recent five-star reviews were read on October 24, 2026, in all languages. Trustpilot labels each review as “Invited”, when the company sent the request, or as organic, when the person came on their own. The table compares the two groups.
postParagraphs: First, five-star reviews arrive much faster and almost all of them by invitation: 100 in about five days, 78 of them invited. One-star reviews take about 18 days to reach 100, and 92 are organic. Our reading: the invitation pushes the average up. The score measures the customers who were invited and answered, not all customers.
Second, one-star reviews are almost four times longer. They describe a concrete problem, with dates, products and amounts. Five-star reviews are usually one sentence.

Third, one in seven one-star reviews in our sample is praise given with the wrong rating: 14 of the 100 have positive text, such as “Great hosting” or “easy to use”, under one star. Even so, 6.9% of 73,411 is still about 5,100 people who were very unhappy. The share is small; the number of people is not.

contentSections.heading: What people complain about
paragraphs: After setting aside the 14 misrated praises, 86 real complaints were left among the 100 most recent one-star reviews. Each complaint was tagged by theme from its title and excerpt, and one complaint can carry more than one theme, so the counts are approximate. These are the themes, from the most to the least cited:
bullets: **AI support and not reaching a person:** about 45 of 86. Part of these are about the AI tools of the website builder, not about support.

**Billing, renewal, refunds and fees:** about 38. This includes the price going up after the promotional period, an automatic renewal the customer did not expect, and the fee to recover an expired domain (76 euros in one review, 150 in another).
**Domains:** about 27, covering suspension, transfer, registration and recovery.
**Site or VPS down, or maintenance without notice:** about 18, including a production VPS stopped for 27 hours.
**Account or service suspended without a clear explanation:** about 16, some of them after a chargeback.
postParagraphs: The most frequent countries among the 100 one-star reviews were the United States (18), India (14), France (8), the United Kingdom (6) and the Netherlands (6).

Trustpilot itself publishes an automatic summary of the profile, generated by the site’s AI from 12,464 reviews. It lists as praise a stable hosting service, helpful support with fast human agents on technical problems, and a panel that is easy for beginners. It lists as complaints a very automated service with difficulty reaching a person, hard account recovery, billing, and strict rules for domain renewal. That matches what we found in the sample.

The first theme deserves a note. In the titles read, the recurring complaint is not a wrong answer but not getting past the AI agent to a person. Our reading: for a customer with a site down, that wait is the problem.
The reviews do not split the billing complaints by reason. The link with automatic renewal is our reading, and it is where the check should start.

contentSections.heading: Why billing weighs on hosting
paragraphs: When automatic renewal is on, the product renews before it expires and is charged to the payment method on file. Hostinger’s help center says so, and also says the option can be turned off at any time, without affecting the service until the expiry date.

Turning renewal off has a risk too: without another plan ready, the site can go offline on the expiry date. That is why the help center itself recommends keeping renewal on for anyone who plans to continue.

The renewal price and what the SONAR20 code covers are in the [SONAR20 coupon article](/en/reviews/hostinger-coupon-code-referral). Here the point is different: knowing where the option is and how to turn it off.

contentSections.heading: How to turn off automatic renewal
paragraphs: According to Hostinger’s help center, read on October 19, 2026, the path is this:
bullets: In your account’s billing area, open the invoices section.
Go to your list of services or subscriptions.
Open the three-dot menu next to the product.
Go to the renewal settings for that product.
Turn off automatic renewal and save the change.
postParagraphs: With the option off, the product stays active until the expiry date. To turn it back on, you need a payment method on file. The help center also says that if renewal is one day or less from expiry, you must renew manually before turning the option back on. Menu names can change, so look for the automatic renewal option in the billing area.

contentSections.heading: What Hostinger answers
paragraphs: On Trustpilot, the company says it responds to 99% of negative reviews, usually within 24 hours. In our sample, 80 of the 86 complaints had a reply; the six without one had all been posted in the previous 24 hours. The page also warns that the company may use AI in its responses.

The replies were counted, not graded, so this text does not say whether the answers solve the problem. Before buying, read a few replies on the profile, especially the ones about billing and about reaching a person.

contentSections.heading: Our experience
paragraphs: Bruno, who also signs this text, has been a Hostinger customer since 2024, for more than 24 months: Business hosting, a KVM 2 VPS, Business email and domains, all with automatic renewal. The Em Casa com Cecília site runs on Hostinger.
Each time he had a problem, support solved it, mainly the AI agent, and he has never seen the service go down.

That is his account, with his use, and it needs an honest counterpoint: the AI support that solved his problems is the theme that shows up most in the complaints read, about 45 of 86, even if part of them are about the AI tools of the website builder. His case says nothing about someone who could not get past the agent, or who was charged without expecting it.

contentSections.heading: Can you trust Hostinger?
paragraphs: Going by Trustpilot, yes. The score was 4.6 from 73,411 reviews, 87.1% of them five stars, and the company answered 99% of the negative ones, 80 of the 86 complaints in our sample.

The caveat is how the score is built and what the complaints say. The profile is managed by the company, which invites customers to review: in our sample, 78 of the 100 most recent five-star reviews were invited and 92 of the 100 most recent one-star reviews were organic. The complaints center on AI support with no way to reach a person, on billing and renewal, and on domains.

In practice: check the renewal date, turn off automatic renewal if you do not want to continue, and read a few one-star reviews and the replies on the profile before buying, because the numbers change every month.

contentSections.heading: Frequently asked questions
bullets: What is Hostinger’s Trustpilot score? A TrustScore of 4.6 out of 5, from 73,411 reviews, with 87.1% five stars and 6.9% one star.

What do Hostinger customers complain about on Trustpilot? In the 86 complaints read among the 100 most recent one-star reviews, the main themes were AI support and not reaching a person (about 45), billing and renewal (about 38) and domains (about 27).

Does Hostinger answer negative reviews? Yes. The page says the company responds to 99% of negative reviews, usually within 24 hours, and may use AI in the replies. In our sample, 80 of 86 complaints had a reply.

How do I turn off Hostinger’s automatic renewal? In your account’s billing area, go to your services, open the three-dot menu next to the product, go to the renewal settings, turn off automatic renewal and save. The product stays active until the expiry date.
